title: Scraper: ASRock Rack (EPYC + WRX80)
description:
Goal: 

Acceptance criteria:
- 

Goal: Scraper for ASRock Rack server motherboards. Distinct corporate entity from consumer ASRock — separate product hierarchy on asrockrack.com but **sharing the same download.asrock.com CDN** as consumer ASRock. Confirmed in survey: consumer scraper's Wayback CDX query captures ASRock Rack BIOSes too, just under different socket folder names.

board_class: EPYC (primary), ThreadripperPro (WRX80D8-2T, WRX80-RUDI, etc.).

Sockets/board families to cover:
- SP3: ROMED8-2T, ROMED8U-2T, EPYCD8-2T, ROMED4ID-2T (Naples/Rome/Milan boards)
- SP5: GENOAD8UD-2T/X550, GENOAD24QM3, GENOAD16TX (Genoa/Bergamo)
- SP6: SIENA-D8 family (Siena)
- sWRX8: WRX80D8-2T, WRX80-RUDI (Threadripper Pro)
- sWRX9 (forthcoming): WRX90 boards

Access strategy:
- Front-end www.asrockrack.com is protected by **Imperva Incapsula** (confirmed during survey — page returned a JS challenge body). Direct scraping is blocked.
- The ASRock CDN at download.asrock.com is *not* WAF-protected and serves both consumer and Rack BIOSes. Wayback CDX query against download.asrock.com/BIOS/* should already return Rack URLs that the consumer scraper currently filters out (only AM4/AM5 socket regex matches today).
- **First task**: run the existing AsRockScraper CDX query without the AM4/AM5 socket filter and inventory which folder names ASRock uses for Rack boards (e.g. SP3, SP5, sWRX80, GENOA, SIENA). Outcome of that inventory drives the parser.
- Fallback if Rack boards live under a separate CDN tree: Wayback CDX against asrockrack.com/sites/default/files/* (typical Drupal upload path) plus download.asrockrack.com.

Implementation notes:
- Strongly recommend a *generalised* AsRockScraper that takes a (socket, board_class) → folder-pattern map, rather than a separate class. The discovery and unwrapping logic is identical to consumer ASRock. Same ZIP layout, same naming.
- Board model names on Rack URLs are unambiguous (ROMED8-2T, GENOAD8UD-2T, WRX80D8-2T) — no chipset-keyword heuristic needed.

License-safe references: none in surveyed prior art covers ASRock Rack.

Acceptance criteria:
- Either generalisation of AsRockScraper or new src/psp_etl/scrape/asrock_rack.py
- CDX inventory documented in commit message or docstring (which folder names exist)
- Tests covering the folder-name → socket mapping
- classify_board_class returns EPYC for SP3/SP5/SP6, ThreadripperPro for sWRX8 (already wired)
- CLI registration

Related: #79, #81.
